IN THE BOOTH

Modeled on a legend

In 1960, White Sox owner Bill Veeck unveiled the first exploding scoreboard at Comiskey Park — a towering bulb-lit board with pinwheels on top that spun, flashed, and set off fireworks every time a Sox player hit a home run. It defined 1970s ballpark showmanship, and its pinwheels still crown the Sox' scoreboard today. This board borrows the whole act: the green steel, the chasing bulbs, the pinwheels — rebuilt clean and modern. (And yes: "Kaminski Park" = Comiskey Park.)

Photos: Baseball History Comes Alive (vintage board) and Ballpark Digest (modern pinwheels).
